classifications.reason: The bicycle contract supplies human-powered wheeled riding, while the required assisting motor and jurisdictional class place admitted members within the quoted ru.electric_bicycle contract.
The bus contract does not require more than three wheels, so the quoted wheel restriction does not establish exclusion.
The class describes a person, whereas the admitting words describe a device upon which a person may ride.
Commercial licensing or a commercial mass classification does not contractually preclude the quoted pedals, seat and low-power motor.
The admitting clause describes electrically assisted bicycles meeting the jurisdiction's three-class requirements, matching the class contract and its taxonomy attribute.
The definition expressly states that the term does not include an electric scooter.
Designation as an emergency vehicle does not impose construction requirements incompatible with the quoted pedals, seat and motor limits.
The fire-fighting vehicle contract specifies no wheel count that conflicts with the quoted two-or-three-wheel requirement.
The definition expressly states that the term does not include a moped.
The contract's exclusion of separately classed powered two-wheelers does not rule out three-wheeled self-propelled members satisfying the quoted equipment limits.
The motorcycle contract permits three-wheeled vehicles ridden astride and does not rule out their having the quoted pedals, saddle and low-power motor.
Official or contracted road service and identifying equipment do not preclude the quoted pedal-equipped, low-power electric construction.
The pedestrian contract describes a person rather than the ridden device described by the admitting words.
The class describes a pedestrian with specified assistance, not a device upon which a person may ride.
The controlling device definition does not exclude rail operation, and the on-track equipment contract does not preclude the quoted pedals, seat and motor.
School designation and jurisdictional markings impose no wheel-count requirement incompatible with the quoted words.
Being a marked passenger vehicle for hire does not contractually prevent satisfaction of the quoted pedal, seat and motor requirements.
The contract's service, body and livery descriptions do not require more than three wheels.
Being drawn by another vehicle or being a combination does not itself preclude possessing the quoted low-power electric motor.
Public transit service and identifying livery or route displays do not establish a wheel count incompatible with the quoted requirement.
The goods-carrying body requirement does not prevent a three-wheeled motor vehicle from satisfying the quoted equipment limits.
